summary: Cross-SDK retry coordination causes duplicate tool/function calls when confirmation tokens are session-scoped
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate external tool invocations when using a mixed-language orchestrator (TS worker + Python worker) that coordinates function calls via Redwood streaming sessions. The duplicates occur on reconnects and during retries.

Impact:
Several production customers using StreamlineDocs experienced duplicated webhook calls and duplicate downstream indexing jobs. This caused out-of-order state in their backend and elevated error rates in their ingest pipeline.

Environment:
- Production cluster us-east-1
- Redwood hosted API, streaming sessions with function-calling enabled
- Customer orchestrator: TS service (v0.13.1) + Python worker (v0.21.4) calling same session id across processes

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Open a streaming session and send a multi-step chat that triggers two function/tool calls in sequence (tool A then tool B).
2) During the response stream, inject a transient network interruption (simulated via tcpkill) causing the TS process to reconnect and resume the session.
3) Orchestrator retries pending steps when unacked for > 2s.
4) Observe duplicate webhook invocations for tool A in the customer backend within 3–6 seconds of reconnect.

Logs / snippets provided by customer:
- TS SDK stream reconnect logs (snippet):
  - [2026-03-01T10:12:05Z] reconnecting session id=abc123 ack_window_ms=2000 nonce=6751
  - [2026-03-01T10:12:06Z] resend pending step id=step-42 confirmation_token=session-6751
- Python SDK worker logs (snippet):
  - [2026-03-01T10:12:06Z] executing tool A id=step-42 confirmation_token=request-7f9d
  - [2026-03-01T10:12:07Z] webhook POST /hooks/toolA 200 OK payload_id=step-42

Notes: the TS SDK was reusing a session-scoped confirmation token on reconnect, while the Python worker generated a per-request confirmation token. The gateway did not have robust dedupe for tokens with mixed scopes.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Patel (customer success): Filed issue after customer escalation; initial triage indicates cross-language token reuse might be root cause.
2026-03-01 - Miguel Torres (assigned): Asking customer for SDK versions, exact headers, and tcpdump of reconnect window. Requested a minimal repro if possible.
2026-03-02 - StreamlineDocs (customer): Provided tcpdump, SDK versions, and a short repro harness. They note that duplicates are rare (1-3% of reconnects) but high-impact.

2026-03-03 - Eng (SRE): Confirmed similar timing in our internal stress test with TS v0.13.1 + Python v0.21.4. Observed interleaved retry scheduling where both sides consider a call unacked and independently execute it.

2026-03-04 - Eng (SDK lead): Noted that TS SDK had an optimization that reuses session-level confirmation tokens for pending batches to reduce header size. This optimization is incompatible with orchestrators that interleave per-request retries from other languages.
investigation: Hypothesis 1: Token-scope mismatch — TS SDK reuses session-scoped confirmation_token on reconnect; Python/Go use request-scoped tokens. When two workers act independently, server-side dedupe cannot distinguish because both tokens are valid but semantically different.

Hypothesis 2: Ack window too aggressive — default ack_window_ms=2000 leads to racing retries on medium-latency hosts; clients schedule retries with jitter that overlaps and causes duplicate external calls.

Data points: Reproduced locally using our stress harness by forcing reconnects. In 1200 trials, duplicate tool calls observed in ~2.1% of reconnects when combining TS v0.13.1 + Python v0.21.4 and ack_window_ms set to 2000. When ack_window_ms increased to 5000 duplicates dropped to 0.1%.

Trace analysis: The TS SDK resend path sets header X-RW-Tool-Confirm: session-6751. Python worker sets X-RW-Tool-Confirm: request-7f9d. Our server dedupe keyed by tool-id + confirmation_token. Because tokens are different, server treats them as separate attempts and forwards both tool invocations to webhook endpoints.
Gateway observation: API gateway normalizes some headers and truncates values > 64 chars; in this case tokens were short so truncation not in play. No 5xx in serving-runtime during tests.

Risk assessment: Medium — occurs only when a single logical workflow is executed by multiple SDK runtimes sharing the same session id and when reconnects overlap the ack window. Many orchestration patterns (microservices handing work to language-specific workers) fit this profile.
resolution:
Short term workaround provided to customer (applied 2026-03-03):
  1) Upgrade TS SDK to v0.13.3 (hotfix) which regenerates per-request confirmation tokens on reconnect (workaround patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ts/pull/4123).
  2) Increase ack_window_ms to 4500 in their session settings to reduce race probability.
  3) Adopt explicit per-action idempotency header X-RW-Tool-Call-Id generated at the orchestrator entry point and pass-through to all workers. Server dedupe also enabled on this header via runtime flag dedupe.header= X-RW-Tool-Call-Id.

Long term fixes and product changes (in flight):
  1) SDK roadmap: standardize confirmation_token scope across SDKs (make per-request the default) and document resumption semantics in SDK READMEs.
  2) Server-side: implement stronger dedupe with canonicalization to accept equivalent tokens (e.g., session-scoped + request-scoped) and server-side best-effort mapping to logical call ids.
  3) Console/runbook: add a runbook page (linked) describing cross-language orchestration patterns and recommended token scheme (per-action idempotency + server dedupe).

Follow-ups/tracking:
  - Backport hotfix to older TS minor branches if customers request.
  - Add an automated integration test that mixes TS/Python/Go SDKs and simulates reconnects to detect regressions.
  - Update public SDK docs with a section "Function-call idempotency patterns for multi-language orchestrators".
